- Build and maintain scalable estimating models and templates while developing detailed bottom-up cost models for complex, site-specific initiatives requiring advanced analytical judgment.

About the Role

As a senior content designer within our Experience Design organization, you will own how our brands sound in the product experience. Across four brands and every stage of the customer journey (discovery, browse, product detail, checkout, post-purchase, and lifecycle) you will write the content customers read, and define the voice, tone, and editorial guidance behind it.

This is a shared capability rather than a role inside a single value stream. You will work across the brand journey leads and the design system team, and you will help decide what content is shared across brands and what stays brand-distinct. Getting there is as much facilitation as writing: sitting with people who have competing brand interests, finding the answer that serves the customer, and writing it down so that it holds.

You will be the first content designer in the function, which means building the practice rather than inheriting one: the guidelines, the content patterns in our design system, and the habit of testing language with customers instead of debating it internally. You will be hands-on throughout, carrying the highest-leverage flows yourself, and you will have support from UX leadership in setting the standard.

The craft we are looking for combines two things. You are deeply human-centered in how you write and think, starting from what the customer is trying to do and what they are unsure about rather than from a brief. You are also comfortable on the technical side: content models, metadata, taxonomy, the constraints a CMS puts on what you can say, localization, and the accessibility of language itself.

You will thrive in an environment where the distance from conversation to prototype to insight is measured in hours, not weeks, and AI is the accelerant. AI will write plausible copy at volume all day, which makes judgment about what is worth saying the scarce skill rather than the throughput. You see AI as a craft multiplier, and you are clear about where human judgment and real customer evidence still have to do the work.

What You'll Do

• Write and edit the content in our customer journey experiences: navigation and labels, product detail, checkout, errors and empty states, and the moments that carry brand personality

• Define voice and tone for our brands in the product experience, and write editorial guidance that people who are not writers can actually use

• Work with the brand journey leads and the design system team to help decide what content is shared across brands and what stays brand-distinct. Facilitate the conversation and document the outcome so it holds

• Build content into the design system: content patterns, component-level guidance, microcopy standards, and the accessibility of language

• Partner with Product Management and Engineering in the value streams so that content is an input to what gets built rather than filled in at the end

• Partner with brand and creative teams so that the product voice and the brand voice are one voice, expressed appropriately for the moment the customer is in

• Partner with UX Research to test language with customers rather than debating it internally. Comprehension, not preference

• Work with structured content: content models, metadata, taxonomy, CMS constraints, and translation and localization readiness

• Raise the standard of content across the team through critique, worked examples, and pairing with designers who are not writers

• Balance scope, business impact, fidelity, and delivery speed on your own work, and say plainly when a trade-off has consequences for the customer

• Measure your work. Connect content decisions to comprehension, task completion, conversion, and support contacts, and use the result to decide what comes next

• Surface where content needs outstrip what one person can cover, so that leadership can see the gaps and plan for them

• Present your work and the reasoning behind it to varied audiences, and take an active part in critique and design review

• Use AI to move faster on drafting, variation, and audit at scale, and be clear about where it helped and where it did not

Who You Are

• Substantial experience in content design or UX writing for consumer-facing digital products, with a portfolio that shows how language changed an experience rather than a collection of writing samples

• An established practitioner with subject matter expertise in your craft, able to own your work end to end without close direction

• Deeply human-centered in how you write and think. You start from what the customer is trying to do and what they are unsure about, and you can show how that changed the words

• You have written voice and tone or editorial guidance that other people actually used. You know the difference between a style guide that sits in a folder and one that changes the work

• Comfortable on the technical side of content: content models, metadata, taxonomy, CMS constraints, localization, and accessibility standards for language

• Creative range. You can write with brand personality and you can write a clear error message, and you know which one the moment calls for

• A facilitator. You are comfortable in a room with competing brand interests, and you can help a group get to an answer rather than a compromise
• Experience across more than one brand or product line. You can say when consistency serves the customer and when brand expression must take priority

• Comfortable working inside a product operating model, partnering with Product Management and Engineering rather than receiving requirements from them

• Data-informed. You test language, you measure what changed, and you can explain the impact to partners in their language

• Hands-on and fast. You are energized by velocity and you use AI to get to evidence sooner without lowering the bar

• Generous with your craft. You raise the standard of writing across designers who are not writers, and you make the people around you better

• Comfortable being the first. You want to build this practice rather than inherit one, and you are candid about what is known and what is not

Department Overview

The Electric Risk Management (ERM) team plays a critical role in evaluating, reporting, and informing investment decisions for PG&E's most significant electric system risks. ERM leads the implementation and continuous improvement of PG&E's risk decision framework, enabling data-driven decision-making across the organization.

The team partners across the Electric Organization to support all aspects of transmission and distribution operations, including system planning, engineering, maintenance, construction, asset management, business planning, emergency response, and system restoration. Through these partnerships, ERM helps ensure that risk considerations are incorporated into strategic, operational, investment, and regulatory decisions.

Position Summary

The Senior Risk Management Analyst is responsible for leading complex analytical efforts that support risk-informed decision-making across PG&E's electric operations. This role develops and applies quantitative risk methodologies to evaluate electric system risks, assess risk mitigation effectiveness, and support investment planning decisions.

The successful candidate will play a key role in advancing PG&E's transition to more granular and integrated risk-based evaluation frameworks that align risk modeling approaches across the enterprise. This position will conduct complex analyses, develop executive-level reporting, support regulatory filings and data requests, and collaborate with stakeholders across multiple organizations to monitor operational and enterprise risks.

The Senior Risk Management Analyst will work closely with Electric Risk Management (ERM), Risk Analytics and Decision Analytics (RADA), Enterprise Operations and Risk Management (EORM), Electric System Planning, Transmission and Distribution Engineering, Electric Asset Strategy, Asset Knowledge Management, Regulatory Affairs, and other business partners to support effective risk management and investment decision-making.

This position is hybrid, working from your remote office and your assigned location once a week and or based on business need.

PG&E is providing the salary range that the company in good faith believes it might pay for this position at the time of the job posting. This compensation range is specific to the locality of the job. The actual salary paid to an individual will be based on multiple factors, including, but not limited to, specific skills, education, licenses or certifications, experience, market value, geographic location, and internal equity. Although we estimate the successful candidate hired into this role will be placed towards the middle or entry point of the range, the decision will be made on a case-by-case basis related to these factors.

Job Responsibilities

• Lead quantitative analyses to support operational, investment, and regulatory risk management strategies within Electric Operations.
• Develop, enhance, and apply risk-based models that inform mitigation strategies, investment prioritization, and operational decision-making.
• Conduct risk assessments for programs, projects, operational processes, and compliance requirements to improve risk visibility and reduce risk exposure.
• Partner with business stakeholders to identify emerging risks, evaluate mitigation alternatives, and develop risk-informed recommendations.
• Support the development, validation, and continuous improvement of electric risk models, including reliability and wildfire risk models.
• Promote data-driven decision-making and advance risk quantification practices across the organization.
• Coordinate with Asset Family Strategists, Regulatory Affairs, Engineering, and Risk Management teams to support risk mitigation planning and execution.
• Analyze and communicate complex risk model outputs and analytical findings to technical and non-technical audiences.

Qualifications

OpenAI is building a new generation of AI-powered consumer devices, creating opportunities to bring increasingly capable AI into people's everyday lives.

Our Data Engineering team is responsible for establishing the foundational data infrastructure that supports the development, manufacturing, launch, and ongoing operation of these products. We're building the systems that connect information across the entire device lifecycle, enabling engineering, operations, and Data Science partners to understand product performance, identify problems, and make better decisions.

This is an early-stage organization with significant greenfield opportunities. We're looking for engineers who want to shape the technical foundations of a rapidly growing business and establish systems that will scale alongside our products.

About the role:

As a Data Engineer, you'll design, build, and scale the data infrastructure that powers OpenAI's hardware and consumer devices organization.

You'll tackle technically challenging problems involving complex data sources, evolving operational requirements, and systems that need to scale from early development through manufacturing and consumer deployment.

Unlike roles focused primarily on supporting individual analytics projects, this position emphasizes building durable, reusable data foundations that enable multiple teams and use cases.

You'll have significant ownership over technical decisions, work closely with partners across engineering, manufacturing, operations, and Data Science, and help define how we approach Data Engineering as the organization grows.

In this role, you will:

- Build foundational data infrastructure: Design and implement reliable, scalable data pipelines, platforms, and datasets that support hardware development, manufacturing, customer operations, and device performance.

- Connect complex data ecosystems: Integrate information across manufacturing systems, factory operations, device telemetry, quality assurance, and customer-facing operational systems.

- Establish durable data models: Develop reusable datasets and data architectures that enable consistent measurement, investigation, and decision-making across multiple teams.

- Enable manufacturing and quality intelligence: Connect manufacturing conditions and production history with downstream product performance, reliability, returns, and failure signals.

- Prepare for scale: Design systems that evolve from early-stage development and initial production to increasingly complex operations and large-scale consumer deployment.

- Partner across disciplines: Work with hardware and software engineers, manufacturing teams, operations leaders, and Data Scientists to translate emerging requirements into robust technical solutions.

- Shape our technical direction: Help establish engineering standards, architectural principles, data quality practices, and infrastructure decisions that will influence the organization for years to come.

You might thrive in this role if you:

- Are comfortable making architectural decisions as requirements evolve and the right solutions aren't immediately obvious.

- Are highly self-directed and can take broad, ambiguous problems from exploration through implementation.

- Enjoy working directly with cross-functional partners and understanding how technical decisions affect real products and operational outcomes.

- Have a builder's mentality and are energized by creating foundational systems rather than exclusively optimizing mature infrastructure.

- Hold a high bar for engineering quality while remaining pragmatic about the speed and flexibility required in an early-stage environment.

Minimum Qualifications:

- Have exceptional Data Engineering fundamentals and a track record of designing, building, and operating complex data systems.

- Bring strong technical judgment around data architecture, distributed systems, data modeling, reliability, and scalability.

- Have experience developing production-grade pipelines and infrastructure across heterogeneous data sources.

- Experience with hardware, consumer electronics, connected devices, or IoT.

- Experience building data infrastructure for manufacturing, factory operations, or supply-chain systems.

- Familiarity with device telemetry, reliability engineering, product quality, or failure analysis.

- Experience supporting customer operations, technical support, or Trust & Safety.

The Nuclear Fuels Engineering (NFE) department is seeking candidates who are passionate about nuclear energy’s role in a clean energy future.
